audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Lazarus, Martha/Mary, resurrection and life I am, Jesus weeping, Lazarus call, council plot, Caiaphas saying, Ephraim withdrawal.

verses.restored: Now a certain one was weak, Lazarus from Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha her sister.

familiar.text: Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.

modern.text: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

original.text: Ἦν δέ τις ἀσθενῶν, Λάζαρος ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: It was Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was weak.

familiar.text: (It was that Mary which anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.)

modern.text: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)

original.text: ἦν δὲ ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ ἀλείψασα τὸν κύριον μύρῳ καὶ ἐκμάξασα τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς, ἧς ὁ ἀδελφὸς Λάζαρος ἠσθένει.

verses.restored: The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, Lord, look, the one you love is weak.

familiar.text: Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.

modern.text: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”

original.text: ἀπέστειλαν οὖν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσαι· Κύριε, ἴδε ὃν φιλεῖς ἀσθενεῖ.

verses.restored: Hearing this, Jesus said, This weakness is not toward death, but for the glory of the Divine, so that the Son of the Divine may be glorified through it.

familiar.text: When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby.

modern.text: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”

original.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Αὕτη ἡ ἀσθένεια οὐκ ἔστιν πρὸς θάνατον ἀλλʼ ὑπὲρ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

familiar.text: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

modern.text: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.

original.text: ἠγάπα δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς καὶ τὸν Λάζαρον.

verses.restored: When therefore he heard that he was weak, he remained two days in the place where he was.

familiar.text: When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was.

modern.text: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,

original.text: ὡς οὖν ἤκουσεν ὅτι ἀσθενεῖ, τότε μὲν ἔμεινεν ἐν ᾧ ἦν τόπῳ δύο ἡμέρας·

verses.restored: Then after this he says to the disciples, Let us go into Judea again.

familiar.text: Then after that saith he to his disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.

modern.text: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”

original.text: ἔπειτα μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν πάλιν.

verses.restored: The disciples say to him, Rabbi, now the Judeans were seeking to stone you, and you are going there again?

familiar.text: His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?

modern.text: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”

original.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Ῥαββί, νῦν ἐζήτουν σε λιθάσαι οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πάλιν ὑπάγεις ἐκεῖ;

verses.restored: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, one does not stumble, because one sees the light of this world.

familiar.text: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Οὐχὶ δώδεκα ⸂ὧραί εἰσιν⸃ τῆς ἡμέρας; ἐάν τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, οὐ προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει·

verses.restored: But if anyone walks in the night, one stumbles, because the light is not in that one.

familiar.text: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no light in him.

modern.text: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”

original.text: ἐὰν δέ τις περιπατῇ ἐν τῇ νυκτί, προσκόπτει, ὅτι τὸ φῶς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: He said these things, and after this he says to them, Lazarus our friend has fallen asleep, but I go so that I may awaken him.

familiar.text: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.

modern.text: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”

original.text: ταῦτα εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάζαρος ὁ φίλος ἡμῶν κεκοίμηται, ἀλλὰ πορεύομαι ἵνα ἐξυπνίσω αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The disciples therefore said to him, Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be saved/healed.

familiar.text: Then said his disciples, Lord, if he sleep, he shall do well.

modern.text: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”

original.text: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ κεκοίμηται σωθήσεται.

verses.restored: Jesus had spoken about his death, but they thought he was speaking about the rest of sleep.

familiar.text: Howbeit Jesus spake of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep.

modern.text: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.

original.text: εἰρήκει δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς περὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ. ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἔδοξαν ὅτι περὶ τῆς κοιμήσεως τοῦ ὕπνου λέγει.

verses.restored: Then Jesus therefore said to them openly, Lazarus died.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.

modern.text: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,

original.text: τότε οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς παρρησίᾳ· Λάζαρος ἀπέθανεν,

verses.restored: And I rejoice for you, so that you may trust, that I was not there. But let us go to him.

familiar.text: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.

modern.text: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”

original.text: καὶ χαίρω διʼ ὑμᾶς, ἵνα πιστεύσητε, ὅτι οὐκ ἤμην ἐκεῖ· ἀλλὰ ἄγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Thomas, called Twin, said to the fellow disciples, Let us also go, so that we may die with him.

familiar.text: Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.

modern.text: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.” Jesus Comforts Martha and Mary

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος τοῖς συμμαθηταῖς· Ἄγωμεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἵνα ἀποθάνωμεν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Coming therefore, Jesus found him already four days having been in the tomb.

familiar.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.

modern.text: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.

original.text: Ἐλθὼν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εὗρεν αὐτὸν τέσσαρας ⸂ἤδη ἡμέρας⸃ ἔχοντα ἐν τῷ μνημείῳ.

verses.restored: Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.

familiar.text: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off:

modern.text: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away,

original.text: ἦν δὲ ⸀ἡ Βηθανία ἐγγὺς τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίων δεκαπέντε.

verses.restored: Many of the Judeans had come to Martha and Mary to console them concerning their brother.

familiar.text: And many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother.

modern.text: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.

original.text: ⸂πολλοὶ δὲ⸃ ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐληλύθεισαν πρὸς ⸀τὴν Μάρθαν καὶ ⸀Μαριὰμ ἵνα παραμυθήσωνται αὐτὰς περὶ τοῦ ⸀ἀδελφοῦ.

verses.restored: Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, met him; but Mary was sitting in the house.

familiar.text: Then Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary sat still in the house.

modern.text: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him; but Mary stayed at home.

original.text: ἡ οὖν Μάρθα ὡς ἤκουσεν ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἔρχεται ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ· ⸀Μαρία δὲ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ ἐκαθέζετο.

verses.restored: Martha said to Jesus, Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

familiar.text: Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

modern.text: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν ⸀ἡ Μάρθα πρὸς ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε ⸂οὐκ ἂν ἀπέθανεν ὁ ἀδελφός μου⸃·

verses.restored: But even now I know that whatever you ask the Divine, the Divine will give you.

familiar.text: But I know, that even now, whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.

modern.text: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ νῦν οἶδα ὅτι ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσῃ τὸν θεὸν δώσει σοι ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Your brother will rise.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.

modern.text: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.

original.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀναστήσεται ὁ ἀδελφός σου.

verses.restored: Martha says to him, I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.

familiar.text: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.

modern.text: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀ἡ Μάρθα· Οἶδα ὅτι ἀναστήσεται ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life; the one trusting into me, even if that one dies, will live.

familiar.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

modern.text: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.

original.text: εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ἀνάστασις καὶ ἡ ζωή· ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ κἂν ἀποθάνῃ ζήσεται,

verses.restored: And everyone living and trusting into me will certainly not die into the age. Do you trust this?

familiar.text: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?

modern.text: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”

original.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ζῶν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· πιστεύεις τοῦτο;

verses.restored: She says to him, Yes, Lord; I have trusted that you are the Messiah, the Son of the Divine, the one coming into the world.

familiar.text: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.

modern.text: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε· ἐγὼ πεπίστευκα ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἐρχόμενος.

verses.restored: Saying this, she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is here and calls you.

familiar.text: And when she had so said, she went her way, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Master is come, and calleth for thee.

modern.text: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”

original.text: Καὶ ⸀τοῦτο εἰποῦσα ἀπῆλθεν καὶ ἐφώνησεν ⸀Μαριὰμ τὴν ἀδελφὴν αὐτῆς λάθρᾳ εἰποῦσα· Ὁ διδάσκαλος πάρεστιν καὶ φωνεῖ σε.

verses.restored: When that one heard, she rose quickly and came to him.

familiar.text: As soon as she heard that, she arose quickly, and came unto him.

modern.text: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.

original.text: ἐκείνη ⸀δὲ ὡς ἤκουσεν ⸀ἠγέρθη ταχὺ καὶ ⸀ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν·

verses.restored: Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.

familiar.text: Now Jesus was not yet come into the town, but was in that place where Martha met him.

modern.text: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.

original.text: οὔπω δὲ ἐληλύθει ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν κώμην, ἀλλʼ ἦν ⸀ἔτι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ὑπήντησεν αὐτῷ ἡ Μάρθα.

verses.restored: The Judeans who were with her in the house consoling her, seeing Mary rise quickly and go out, followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb to weep there.

familiar.text: The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goeth unto the grave to weep there.

modern.text: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.

original.text: οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι οἱ ὄντες μετʼ αὐτῆς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ παραμυθούμενοι αὐτήν, ἰδόντες τὴν ⸀Μαριὰμ ὅτι ταχέως ἀνέστη καὶ ἐξῆλθεν, ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῇ ⸀δόξαντες ὅτι ὑπάγει εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον ἵνα κλαύσῃ ἐκεῖ.

verses.restored: Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was and saw him, fell at his feet, saying to him, Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

familiar.text: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

modern.text: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”

original.text: ἡ οὖν ⸀Μαριὰμ ὡς ἦλθεν ὅπου ⸀ἦν Ἰησοῦς ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἔπεσεν αὐτοῦ ⸀πρὸς τοὺς πόδας, λέγουσα αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ἦς ὧδε οὐκ ἄν ⸂μου ἀπέθανεν⸃ ὁ ἀδελφός.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore, when he saw her weeping and the Judeans who came with her weeping, was deeply moved in spirit and troubled himself.

familiar.text: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,

modern.text: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.

original.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ὡς εἶδεν αὐτὴν κλαίουσαν καὶ τοὺς συνελθόντας αὐτῇ Ἰουδαίους κλαίοντας ἐνεβριμήσατο τῷ πνεύματι καὶ ἐτάραξεν ἑαυτόν,

verses.restored: He said, Where have you laid him? They say to him, Lord, come and see.

familiar.text: And said, Where have ye laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see.

modern.text: “Where have you put him?” He asked. “Come and see, Lord,” they answered.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν· Ποῦ τεθείκατε αὐτόν; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.

verses.restored: Jesus wept.

familiar.text: Jesus wept.

modern.text: Jesus wept.

original.text: ἐδάκρυσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: The Judeans therefore were saying, See how he loved him.

familiar.text: Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!

modern.text: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”

original.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἴδε πῶς ἐφίλει αὐτόν.

verses.restored: But some of them said, Could not this one, who opened the eyes of the blind, also have made it so this one would not die?

familiar.text: And some of them said, Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?

modern.text: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?” Jesus Raises Lazarus (Acts 9:36–43)

original.text: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἐδύνατο οὗτος ὁ ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ποιῆσαι ἵνα καὶ οὗτος μὴ ἀποθάνῃ;

verses.restored: Jesus therefore, again deeply moved in himself, comes to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it.

familiar.text: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.

modern.text: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.

original.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν πάλιν ἐμβριμώμενος ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔρχεται εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· ἦν δὲ σπήλαιον, καὶ λίθος ἐπέκειτο ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Jesus says, Take away the stone. Martha, the sister of the one who had died, says to him, Lord, by now there will be odor, for it is the fourth day.

familiar.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.

modern.text: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said. “Lord, by now he stinks,” said Martha, the sister of the dead man. “It has already been four days.”

original.text: λέγει ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρατε τὸν λίθον. λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τοῦ ⸀τετελευτηκότος Μάρθα· Κύριε, ἤδη ὄζει, τεταρταῖος γάρ ἐστιν.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Did I not say to you that if you trust, you will see the glory of the Divine?

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶπόν σοι ὅτι ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς ⸀ὄψῃ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.restored: They took away the stone. Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, Father, I thank you that you heard me.

familiar.text: Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.

modern.text: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.

original.text: ἦραν οὖν τὸν ⸀λίθον. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἄνω καὶ εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι ἤκουσάς μου,

verses.restored: I knew that you always hear me, but because of the crowd standing around I said it, so that they may trust that you sent me.

familiar.text: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.

modern.text: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”

original.text: ἐγὼ δὲ ᾔδειν ὅτι πάντοτέ μου ἀκούεις· ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον τὸν περιεστῶτα εἶπον, ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.

verses.restored: Saying these things, he cried out with a great voice, Lazarus, come out.

familiar.text: And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

modern.text: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

original.text: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐκραύγασεν· Λάζαρε, δεῦρο ἔξω.

verses.restored: The one who had died came out, bound feet and hands with burial cloths, and his face wrapped in a cloth. Jesus says to them, Loose him and let him go.

familiar.text: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

modern.text: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. “Unwrap him and let him go,” Jesus told them. The Plot to Kill Jesus (Matthew 26:1–5; Mark 14:1–2; Luke 22:1–2)

original.text: ⸀ἐξῆλθεν ὁ τεθνηκὼς δεδεμένος τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας κειρίαις, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ σουδαρίῳ περιεδέδετο. λέγει ⸂αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἄφετε ⸀αὐτὸν ὑπάγειν.

verses.restored: Therefore many of the Judeans who had come to Mary and beheld what he did trusted into him.

familiar.text: Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him.

modern.text: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.

original.text: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς τὴν ⸀Μαριὰμ καὶ θεασάμενοι ⸀ἃ ⸀ἐποίησεν, ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν·

verses.restored: But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

familiar.text: But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done.

modern.text: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

original.text: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπῆλθον πρὸς τοὺς Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς ἃ ⸀ἐποίησεν Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: Therefore the chief priests and Pharisees gathered a council and were saying, What are we doing? For this human does many signs.

familiar.text: Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles.

modern.text: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.

original.text: συνήγαγον οὖν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συνέδριον, καὶ ἔλεγον· Τί ποιοῦμεν ὅτι οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος πολλὰ ⸂ποιεῖ σημεῖα⸃;

verses.restored: If we leave him thus, all will trust into him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and nation.

familiar.text: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.

modern.text: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”

original.text: ἐὰν ἀφῶμεν αὐτὸν οὕτως, πάντες πιστεύσουσιν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐλεύσονται οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι καὶ ἀροῦσιν ἡμῶν καὶ τὸν τόπον καὶ τὸ ἔθνος.

verses.restored: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, You know nothing,

familiar.text: And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,

modern.text: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!

original.text: εἷς δέ τις ἐξ αὐτῶν Καϊάφας, ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε οὐδέν,

verses.restored: nor do you reason that it is advantageous for you that one human should die for the people, and not the whole nation perish.

familiar.text: Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.

modern.text: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”

original.text: οὐδὲ ⸀λογίζεσθε ὅτι συμφέρει ⸀ὑμῖν ἵνα εἷς ἄνθρωπος ἀποθάνῃ ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ ἔθνος ἀπόληται.

verses.restored: He did not say this from himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation,

familiar.text: And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation;

modern.text: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,

original.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ οὐκ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ ἀρχιερεὺς ὢν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου ἐπροφήτευσεν ὅτι ἔμελλεν Ἰησοῦς ἀποθνῄσκειν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους,

verses.restored: and not for the nation only, but also so that the scattered children of the Divine might be gathered into one.

familiar.text: And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.

modern.text: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.

original.text: καὶ οὐχ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἔθνους μόνον, ἀλλʼ ἵνα καὶ τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ τὰ διεσκορπισμένα συναγάγῃ εἰς ἕν.

verses.restored: From that day therefore they took counsel to kill him.

familiar.text: Then from that day forth they took counsel together for to put him to death.

modern.text: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.

original.text: ἀπʼ ἐκείνης οὖν τῆς ἡμέρας ⸀ἐβουλεύσαντο ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore no longer walked openly among the Judeans, but went away from there into the region near the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there he remained with the disciples.

familiar.text: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews; but went thence unto a country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there continued with his disciples.

modern.text: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.

original.text: ⸂Ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς⸃ οὐκέτι παρρησίᾳ περιεπάτει ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν χώραν ἐγγὺς τῆς ἐρήμου, εἰς Ἐφραὶμ λεγομένην πόλιν, κἀκεῖ ⸀ἔμεινεν μετὰ τῶν ⸀μαθητῶν.

verses.restored: The Passover of the Judeans was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the country before the Passover to purify themselves.

familiar.text: And the Jews’ passover was nigh at hand: and many went out of the country up to Jerusalem before the passover, to purify themselves.

modern.text: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.

original.text: Ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβησαν πολλοὶ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐκ τῆς χώρας πρὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἵνα ἁγνίσωσιν ἑαυτούς.

verses.restored: They were seeking Jesus and saying with one another as they stood in the temple, What do you think? That he will certainly not come to the feast?

familiar.text: Then sought they for Jesus, and spake among themselves, as they stood in the temple, What think ye, that he will not come to the feast?

modern.text: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”

original.text: ἐζήτουν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔλεγον μετʼ ἀλλήλων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστηκότες· Τί δοκεῖ ὑμῖν; ὅτι οὐ μὴ ἔλθῃ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν;

verses.restored: Now the chief priests and Pharisees had given commands that if anyone knew where he was, that one should report it, so that they might seize him.

familiar.text: Now both the chief priests and the Pharisees had given a commandment, that, if any man knew where he were, he should shew it, that they might take him.

modern.text: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.

original.text: δεδώκεισαν ⸀δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ⸀ἐντολὰς ἵνα ἐάν τις γνῷ ποῦ ἐστιν μηνύσῃ, ὅπως πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.
